why: Paper 1: calibrating Hartree–Fock against the local exchange on an f block we can measure, ours Cs–Hf (Z = 55–72). In 4D Hartree–Fock separates f-row configurations by 5–9 eV and disagrees with the local exchange on elements 107–111; ours has no f block in the baked table, so atom/tools/hftable.mjs rank now seeds Z > 36 from the measured configurations in papers/p1/data/nist-lanthanides.json (NIST Handbook). Each element: the local-exchange search's settled candidates within 4 eV, each solved by js/hf.js with the full term correction (europium took 3.4 min here).
